description.short: The second highest grade of white tea — one bud with two leaves, richer and fruitier than Silver Needle
description.overview: More accessible and full-flavored than Bai Hao Yin Zhen due to the presence of tender leaves alongside buds, giving the liquor a rounder, fuller body.
description.leaf: Downy bud flanked by two grayish-green leaves
description.liquor: Light golden liquor, slightly deeper than Silver Needle
description.aroma: Floral, fruity, with hints of fresh hay
description.taste: Smooth, with gentle fruity sweetness and delicate astringency
description.processing: Plucking one bud with two leaves → extended natural withering in sun and shade → slow drying without fixation or rolling

history.origin: The name means 'White Peony' — referring to the look of the dried leaves opening up like a flower during brewing.
history.development: Began widespread production in the early 20th century as a more accessible alternative to costly Silver Needle, utilizing less rigid plucking standards.
history.modern: Today, it is one of the most popular and recognized white teas internationally thanks to its balance of quality, flavor, and affordability.
interestingFacts: There is an internal grading hierarchy for Bai Mu Dan (Premium, Grade 1, Grade 2) based on the proportion of buds to leaves in the plucked tea.
Like other white teas, it ages exceptionally well, gradually developing a richer, warmer, honeyed profile over years of storage.
